records.statement: A BuildKit-only build flag (`--cache-to`) is accepted and passed through, and the build still produces the configured image.
records.notes: deacon-only surface. Scoped deliberately to acceptance and pass-through: on Docker 29.6.2 with the default `docker` driver a local cache export writes nothing observable, so whether the cache was WRITTEN is not a claim this can make and is not made.

records.statement: A Dockerfile instruction that exits non-zero fails the build, and the failure is reported at the build stage rather than as a later container-creation failure.
records.notes: The exit code alone cannot distinguish a build failure from a container-creation failure; the declared failure phase is what makes the two different facts rather than the same number.

records.statement: `build` reports and tags the FEATURE-EXTENDED image, so a user-supplied `--image-name` resolves to the image with the Features installed rather than to the pre-Feature base.
records.notes: This project shipped the inverse once: the post-build Feature pass layered correctly and the user's tag still pointed at the base, which every outcome-only assertion reported as success. The case pins the reported image AND the tag in one ordered match.

records.statement: `build` stamps `org.deacon.configHash` on the image it produces; the reference CLI sets no such label.
records.notes: Measured against oracle 0.87.0 on fx-build-image-labels and fx-build-image-args, not inferred. A deacon-only bookkeeping label in deacon's own `org.deacon.*` namespace — the reference has no concept of it, so there is nothing to diverge from. Recorded by ext-build-image-bookkeeping-label and tolerated per-key on the two differential cases; the tolerance names the ONE key, never a namespace. Distinct from bhv-container-identity-labels, which describes five labels on a created CONTAINER in the `devcontainer.*` namespace.

records.statement: The `devcontainer.metadata` label on a BUILT image records one entry per installed Feature plus the configuration pick, so a later consumer of the image can read what it carries.
records.notes: OPEN — filed as #436. Measured against oracle 0.87.0 on fx-build-dockerfile-feature: the reference writes `[ {"id":"./features/marker"} ]` and deacon writes `[{"configHash":"dd386475bebe4dcf"}]`. deacon's `build` path hardcodes the value at crates/deacon/src/commands/build/mod.rs:2056 under a comment naming it a simplification, so every Feature entry is dropped and `configHash` — not a devcontainer.json property — stands in their place. NOT a computation defect: the SAME fixture through `deacon up` writes the correct `[{"id":"./features/marker"}]` on the container, and crates/core/src/build/metadata.rs already builds the right value; the build command simply does not use it. Deliberately NOT waived: the two differential cases carry no tolerance for this key, so they report the divergence until the fix lands and go green when it does. Distinct from bhv-container-metadata-label-serialization (#394), which is about the value's BYTE FORM, not its entries.

records.statement: build produces a container image and reports the build outcome, matching the reference.
records.notes: Backed by case-build-image-labels-differential and case-build-image-args-differential, which compare the produced IMAGE's whole configuration between the two CLIs. Until the built-image observation capability existed the only evidence was `parity_build`, a hand-written carrier that could ask whether an image existed but not what was in it.

records.statement: The image a `build` produces carries what the configuration and Dockerfile authored into it — labels, environment, command and working directory — and `build.args` reach the build so an arg-derived value is the configured one rather than the Dockerfile default.
records.notes: Measured against oracle 0.87.0 on fx-build-image-labels and fx-build-image-args: `Env`, `Cmd`, `Entrypoint`, `WorkingDir` and every authored label agree exactly on both fixtures, including `parity.build.arg=passed-from-config` (a build that dropped `build.args` would leave the Dockerfile default `default-not-passed` and is the failure this distinguishes). The two labels that do NOT agree are recorded separately: `org.deacon.configHash` (bhv-build-image-bookkeeping-label, a deacon extension) and `devcontainer.metadata` (bhv-build-image-metadata-label, a deacon defect, #436). Observing the produced IMAGE rather than a container is what makes this checkable at all — a `build` leaves no container, so every earlier assertion on this behavior could only read the CLI's own stdout.

records.statement: `build --output type=docker,dest=<path>` exports the built image to that path and reports the export destination.
records.notes: deacon-only surface: the reference CLI has no `--output` flag on `build`, so there is nothing to compare against and the case is a spec-expectation. The claim pinned is the ARTIFACT (the tar exists), not the echoed `exportPath` — a build that accepted the flag and wrote nothing satisfies the echo.

records.statement: `build --platform <os/arch>` builds for the named platform and produces a real image carrying the configuration's authored labels.
records.notes: deacon-only surface (`--platform` is not a reference `build` flag). Previously covered by an assertion that tolerated either outcome and therefore asserted nothing on any machine with BuildKit; now pinned to success plus the produced image's labels.

records.statement: `build --push` to a registry that cannot be reached fails with a non-zero exit and a diagnostic naming the push as the failing step, rather than reporting success.
records.notes: Both CLIs fail non-zero and name the push. deacon's message currently names the WRONG registry — it pushes its internal `deacon-build:<hash>` tag, which resolves to Docker Hub, and that push fails before the user's registry is contacted (#438, measured against oracle 0.87.0, which tags only the user's `--image-name`). The case asserts the part that is right and stays true across the fix.

records.statement: `build --push` pushes the image names the user supplied and nothing else.
records.notes: OPEN — filed as #438. Measured against oracle 0.87.0 on fx-build-flags with `--push --image-name registry.invalid/conformance-push:latest`: deacon also tags the image with its internal deterministic `deacon-build:<hash>`, which has no registry component and so resolves to `docker.io/library/`, and BuildKit pushes it — the failure reported is a Docker Hub authorization error for a command that named a private registry, and the named registry is never contacted. The reference passes only `-t registry.invalid/conformance-push:latest` and fails against that host. On a machine holding Docker Hub credentials for a matching repository this would upload an image the user never asked to publish. `case-build-push-unreachable-registry` asserts the part that is already right (non-zero exit, a diagnostic naming the push) and stays true across the fix.
